messages:
Priya: heads up — incident-bot just fired a P1 for cross-region routing errors in eu-west and us-east. 503 spikes, customer impact reports from a few enterprise tenants.
incident-bot: [ALERT] service: redwood-router  severity: P1  regions: eu-west, us-east  recent errors: 84%  action: paging oncall
Tom: I’m on my commute but can jump in. primary is Ana, right? Ana (oncall): I am primary for this shift. currently pulling up metrics and the router logs. seeing a sharp rise in 503s from the gw-tier.
Ana (oncall): quick check — can someone confirm if there was a config roll in the last 20m in us-east? ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: deploy/redwood-router v2.14.1 -> started 3632109500 by tom.deploy; finished 3632109640; no rollback recorded.
Priya: that deploy timestamp aligns. maybe regression. Ana (oncall): OK I'm calling the runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/router-p1 — starting checklist. @Mika do we want to escalate to infra immediately or try quick mitigation?
Mika (SRE-Lead): escalate. router is core. page infra and network. if primary is blocked, page secondary. Tom: paging infra now — paging list: @infra-oncall, @network-oncall, @db-oncall. sending summons.
Tom: /page infra-oncall "P1 redwood-router 503 spike us-east/eu-west — deploy at 3632109500 suspected; primary Ana engaged; need rollback permission or traffic-split. join bridge: https://meet.red/3632109876"
Priya: note: some customers reported degraded embeddings throughput — could be cascading. putting a short note to CS channel.
Ana (oncall): quick mitigation idea: set routing weight to favor us-west-only for affected model-serving routes to reduce cross-region pressure. That avoids full rollback. thoughts?
Mika (SRE-Lead): good plan if it reduces error rate quickly. get infra to apply traffic-split and have deploy owner prepare rollback artifact. Tom: infra acknowledged, they’ll try weighted routing change.
ops-bot: infra-oncall acknowledged the page at 3632109902 and joined bridge.
Ana (oncall): applying temporary routing rule now (using ctl). snippet I’m running: 
```
# reduce cross-region to us-west primary, 80% us-west, 20% others
redwoodctl routing update --service router --route "/model/*" --weights us-west=0.8,us-east=0.1,eu-west=0.1
```
Ana (oncall): applied at 3632109975. watching metrics.
Priya: watch latency for us-west saturation, but better than 503s.
Tom: infra confirms weighted routing applied and error rate dropped to 12% in eu-west within 90s. us-west latency +20ms but stable.
Mika (SRE-Lead): good. next steps: keep mitigation for 30 minutes while we analyze logs and decide rollback vs fix forward. also collect correlation ids for affected requests for customer communication. Ana, can you collect top failing traces?
Ana (oncall): grabbing top traces now. command: 
```
redwoodctl traces query --service router --since 15m --filter status=503 --group-by request.path --top 50
```
Ana (oncall): found a pattern: requests with long prompt tokens (~>12k) correlate with KV cache overflow errors on the gw-tier. opening a ticket to runtime team.
Tom: paging runtime team: @runtime-oncall — please join, possible KV cache bug.
incident-bot: page sent to runtime-oncall at 3632110170
Mika (SRE-Lead): if runtime can't fix quickly, we need a short-term config: cap token length or reject >10k prompts with 429 and adapted error message to upstream clients. Priya, can you draft the customer-facing status and ask CS to notify affected customers with mitigations?
Priya: on it. Draft: "We're currently mitigating a routing/kv-cache issue affecting a subset of multi-region requests; we've applied a temporary routing adjustment to reduce errors. Engineering is investigating root cause; we'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Sending to #customer-success now.
Ana (oncall): runtime-oncall joined bridge and confirmed investigateable bug in kv-cache eviction. runtime suggests a quick server-side guard to return 429 for requests >10k tokens or apply a graceful reject for streaming sessions. They can ship a hotfix in ~45m if infra keeps the routing mitigation.
Mika (SRE-Lead): approve guard if runtime can ship a non-breaking guard. Tom: coordinate with infra for canary rollout and ensure canary matches traffic from affected tenants only.
Tom: infra will canary the guard for 10% traffic in us-west. if green for 10m then ramp.
Ana (oncall): updating runbook status: mitigation applied (routing weight), runtime hotfix in flight, runtime guard canary scheduled. bridging notes posted.
Priya: CS updated customers and added a link to status page. tagging legal for any contract-sensitive tenants.
Mika (SRE-Lead): decision log: mitigation-first (routing), then guard canary, then rollback if guard fails. no full rollback now. escalate to execs if impact >5% customer error budget sustained 30m.
Ana (oncall): will keep monitoring. if primary becomes unreachable, Tom you’re listed as secondary for this shift — confirm you'll continue if I need to step away.
Tom: confirmed. if needed I'll take over.
incident-bot: incident updated: P1 -> mitigation in place; next update at 3632110800 or on-change.
Ana (oncall): thanks team. I'll add detailed runbook steps and post postmortem template link once we stabilize: https://internal.redwood/postmortems/template. closing handoff notes for next shift.
Mika (SRE-Lead): one last ask — tag the routing and runtime PRs with the incident id and attach to postmortem. good job on quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
